title: National Celebrations on World Elephant Day 2026 held at Visakhapatnam; Gaj Gaurav Awards 2026 conferred for Exemplary Contributions to Elephant Conservation and Management
subtitle:
India’s commitment to Elephant Conservation is not merely a Policy Choice, but a Reflection of Civilizational Values and Ecological Responsibility: MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh

‘Conflict to Coexistence’ is the motto of the State Government in addressing the Human-Elephant Conflict cases: Dy. CM (Andhra Pradesh), Shri K. Pawan Kalyan

MoS (EFCC) chaired 23rd Steering Committee Meeting of Project Elephant; Workshop on ‘Human–Elephant Conflict: varying scenarios Across India’ organised

Regional Action Plan for Comprehensive Understanding and Management of Human–Elephant Conflict in Southern India released
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoS, EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, presided over the national celebrations of World Elephant Day 2026 at Visakhapatnam today. Shri Konidala Pawan Kalyan, Deputy Chief Minister (Andhra Pradesh), graced the occasion as the Guest of Honour. The event saw participation of Shri Tanmay Kumar, Secretary (EFCC), Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi, DG (Forest) and Special Secretary; Shri Ramesh Pandey, ADG (Wildlife), besides senior officers of the Ministry, and Andhra Pradesh Forest Department. Officers from the Ministry of Railways, State Forest Departments, scientific institutions and other stakeholders were also present during the event.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is pioneering a sustainable future for elephants by combining cutting-edge technologies like AI, remote sensing and geospatial mapping with traditional knowledge to protect their habitats. He further underlined the need for cross-sectoral engagement, community participation and scientific approaches to reduce Human–Elephant Conflict (HEC) while ensuring the well-being of local communities.
Shri Singh stated that India’s commitment to elephant conservation is not merely a policy choice, but a reflection of our civilizational values and ecological responsibility. He highlighted that with 33 Elephant Reserves, 150 scientifically identified elephant corridors and nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephant population, India continues to play a leading role in elephant conservation. HEC is a complex issue and it requires a coordinated solution by including various stakeholders and utilising scientific data after its ground-level validation, the Minister added.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri Konidala Pawan Kalyan, Deputy Chief Minister (Andhra Pradesh), informed that ‘Conflict to Coexistence’ is the motto of the State Government in addressing the HEC cases, considering it as a shared responsibility beyond States’ administrative boundaries. He also talked about the H.A.N.U.M.A.N. (Healing And Nurturing Units for Monitoring, Aid and Nursing of Wildlife) initiative of the Andhra Pradesh Government and how the State Government is using modern technology and engaging with local communities, besides capacity building of frontline forest staff in protecting wildlife in the State.
As part of the national celebrations, Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh conferred
Gaj Gaurav Awards 2026
to individuals for their exemplary contributions to elephant conservation and management.
A key highlight of the event was the release of
30 Giant Steps
, highlighting 30 major milestones, achievements and conservation initiatives undertaken under Project Elephant during 2020–2026. Launched in 1992 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, Project Elephant has completed more than three decades of dedicated efforts towards protecting elephants, their habitats and corridors, addressing HEC and ensuring the welfare of captive elephants.
Another significant release was the
Regional Action Plan for Comprehensive Understanding and Management of Human–Elephant Conflict in Southern India
(Karnataka, Keralam, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu). Prepared under the Project Elephant in consultation with the Southern elephant range States, scientific institutions and subject experts, the Plan adopts a landscape-level approach to address HEC across the region. The Plan, with a support of Rs. 500 crores from the Government of India, focuses on habitat connectivity, corridor conservation, early-warning systems, conflict mitigation infrastructure, habitat restoration, community participation, research and monitoring, rapid response mechanisms, capacity building and strengthened interstate coordination.
The event also marked the release of a
Special Issue of the
Journal of Wildlife Science
commemorating three decades of elephant conservation in India. The Special Issue brings together scientific knowledge and research generated over the past three decades to support future management and conservation of elephants under Project Elephant. The
monograph
,
‘Asian Elephants in Central India Before 1947’
, was also released, providing an important historical account of elephant distribution, status and the human–elephant interface in Central India.
The
23rd Steering Committee Meeting of Project Elephant
, chaired by Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, was also held at Visakhapatnam. The meeting deliberated on current issues in elephant conservation and management and witnessed the release of key initiatives and publications, including The Trumpet, Volume VI Issue 01; the Model Elephant Conservation Plan for the Nilgiri Elephant Reserve; ‘Captive Elephant Husbandry: Science, Welfare and Practice’; and the
Phase II of Human Elephant conflict study
- Keralam, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and West Bengal. These initiatives further strengthen evidence-based conservation, captive elephant welfare and landscape-level HEC management.
A
Workshop on ‘Human–Elephant Conflict: Varying Scenarios Across India’
was also organised as part of the celebrations, bringing together regulatory authorities, scientific institutions and field agencies from elephant-range States. It reviewed the status, trends and regional variations of HEC through scientific evidence, long-term datasets and field experiences. Discussions focused on innovative policies, technologies and best practices for conflict mitigation, including veterinary interventions, prevention of electrocution and railway-related elephant mortality, habitat and corridor management, and integrated landscape approaches. The workshop also emphasised strengthening collaboration among the MoEFCC, State Forest Departments, research institutions, Indian Railways and other stakeholders for coordinated, science-based strategies to promote human–elephant coexistence.
As part of the nationwide celebrations, the Project Elephant, in coordination with National Museum of Natural History, organised a
mass awareness campaign
across the country. The campaign witnessed participation of more than 20 lakh students from 21,450 schools. Painting and mask-making competitions, rallies, nukkad nataks, awareness programmes and pledge-taking ceremonies were organised to sensitise children about the ecological and cultural significance of elephants and the importance of protecting their habitats. Students across the country also took a pledge to protect and conserve elephants, reaffirming their commitment to becoming young ambassadors for wildlife and environmental conservation.
The World Elephant Day 2026 celebrations in Visakhapatnam reaffirmed India’s commitment to securing the future of its national heritage animal through science, technology, habitat and corridor conservation, community participation and coordinated action, ensuring that future generations inherit healthy elephant populations and resilient forest landscapes.

title: National Biodiversity Authority releases Rs. 15.52 crore ABS Proceeds from Mustard Genetic Resources
subtitle: Amount to be shared among 26 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils based on Mustard cultivation area
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 8:44AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has released Rs. 15.52 crore in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) proceeds from M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation, which developed ten commercial mustard (Brassica juncea) hybrid varieties using India's biological resources. The amount will flow to 26 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), with the ABS share calculated based on the area under mustard cultivation in each State.
M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation bred the ten varieties in-house but the parental lines were sourced from the open market and traders. As no single farmer or community could be identified as the source, the NBA constituted an Expert Committee to work out the modalities for ABS disbursal in such cases.
The modalities suggested by the Expert Committee were approved by the Authority. Accordingly, in cases where biological resources are accessed from intermediaries, the ABS is to be shared among the SBBs/UTBCs where the resource is cultivated. The NBA sourced cultivation-area figures from the ICAR–Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (ICAR-IIRMR), Bharatpur, Rajasthan, and used them to calculate each State's share.
Rajasthan, which accounts for nearly 42 per cent of India's mustard cultivation, is receiving the highest benefit, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. As mustard cultivation is spread across the country, almost every State and Union Territory receives a share proportionately. The top ten ABS receiving States are:

Every SBB and UTBC has to utilise the ABS amount as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, which includes conservation-linked work; documenting and updating People's Biodiversity Registers; in-situ and ex-situ conservation of biodiversity; restoring degraded ecosystems; strengthening Biodiversity Heritage Sites; building the capacity of Biodiversity Management Committees; improving community livelihoods, among other activities.
The release is part of the NBA's ongoing effort under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, to ensure that when India's genetic resources create commercial value, a fair share flows back to conservation and to the States and communities that sustain that diversity, in line with the Nagoya Protocol and Target 13 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on fair and equitable benefit sharing.
The NBA has released a total ABS amount of Rs. 182.5 crore so far. It has released Rs. 116.22 crore to beneficiaries across the country in the last 12 months.
About the National Biodiversity Authority
The National Biodiversity Authority is a statutory body established under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, functioning under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. It regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol's principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.

title: DRI busts illegal drug manufacturing facility in Jewar, UP; 30 kg drugs seized and two persons arrested
subtitle: 30 kg precursor chemicals to be used for manufacture of drugs, and complete equipment and apparatus also seized
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has busted another clandestine drug manufacturing facility. The facility was found operating from a residential premises in the Jewar area of Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.
On 09/10 Aug 2026, an intelligence-led operation of DRI, resulted in the seizure of approximately
30 kg Amphetamine/intermediary forms, around 30 kg precursor chemicals, to be used for manufacture of drugs,
and complete equipment and apparatus used for clandestine manufacture of psychotropic substances.
Various chemicals, equipment and contraband recovered from the premise.
Search of the premises revealed a
fully equipped clandestine manufacturing set-up
, comprising electrical furnaces, hose pipes, scientific and measuring equipment, reagents and other equipment and tools required for manufacture of psychotropic substances. Multiple liquid containers containing various precursor chemicals, raw materials and reagents were also recovered from the premises, along with white-coloured powdery/crystalline substances stored in different containers, whose testing with field kits indicated the presence of
amphetamine
, a psychotropic substance scheduled under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985.
The recoveries, along with the manufacturing apparatus, amphetamine and chemicals found at the premises, indicate the existence of a clandestine facility being used for illicit manufacture of psychotropic substances in contravention of the provisions of the (NDPS) Act, 1985.  A foreign national and his Indian female associate, who were operating the clandestine facility, were arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.
Preliminary investigation indicated the accused persons would bring manufacturing equipment and raw materials to the premises during night hours, set up and operate the facility for about a week, and thereafter would remove the equipment and clean the premises. The same cycle was reportedly repeated after a gap of two to three months, apparently to avoid suspicion among local residents.
Recent DRI action against clandestine drug manufacturing
The present operation is result of DRI's intensified focus on dismantling clandestine drug manufacturing infrastructure and the networks supporting illicit production and trafficking.
In the past one month, DRI has busted three other clandestine manufacturing facilities
—a
Mephedrone manufacturing facility
at Ankleshwar, Gujarat, where Mephedrone and substantial quantities of precursor chemicals were seized and three persons arrested; an
Alprazolam and Diazepam manufacturing facility
in Satara, Maharashtra, where finished and intermediary psychotropic substances and approximately 400 litres of raw materials were seized and two persons arrested; and a
Tramadol manufacturing
and export network centred in Ambernath, Maharashtra, linked to an attempted export of 1 lakh Tramadol to Nigeria, resulting in the arrest of three key accused persons.
These successive operations demonstrate DRI's continued focus on identifying and dismantling the entire ecosystem of illicit drug manufacture—from procurement of precursor chemicals and establishment of clandestine laboratories to financing, trafficking, storage and attempted export of narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances. The operations also highlight the increasingly sophisticated methods adopted by drug trafficking networks to conceal manufacturing activities and evade detection.

title: Two-day ICMR-SHINE 2026 concludes, igniting scientific curiosity across thousands of young minds
subtitle:
From remote terrains to rural regions, ICMR-SHINE takes biomedical research closer to young minds across 83 locations in 31 States and Union Territories, contributing to a Swasth and Viksit Bharat

Students gain first-hand exposure to Mobile BSL-3 laboratories in Nagpur and Gorakhpur, live scientific demonstrations and hands-on activities nationwide

Young innovators showcase public health solutions through Atal Tinkering Labs in Delhi

ICMR launched SHINE website and announced nationwide school competition on real-world public health challenges, with applications open till 11 September 2026

Schools and teachers welcome research exposure, call for more frequent engagement with students
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Health Research - Indian Council of Medical Research (DHR-ICMR) successfully concluded the second edition of ICMR-SHINE (Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers) on 11–12 August 2026, bringing the world of biomedical and public health research closer to school students across the country. Taking forward the Prime Minister’s call to “spend a day as a scientist,” the nationwide outreach program opened the doors of ICMR laboratories to students of Classes 9 to 12, giving them an opportunity to see, experience, and interact directly with the science behind public health.
The initiative spanned 31 States and Union Territories across 83 unique locations, stretching far beyond major metropolitan centers into the quiet valleys and remote terrains of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Andamans and rural regions of Jharkand, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh. For thousands of students who had never experienced research environment, ICMR-SHINE offered a welcoming bridge into the world of biomedical inquiry. Guided by Dr Curio, the friendly official mascot featured across interactive videos, posters, and cut-outs, the atmosphere was designed to make complex science feel inviting, accessible, and fun.
In Nagpur and Gorakhpur, students stepped near state-of-the-art Mobile BSL-3 laboratories on wheels, witnessing firsthand how high-containment research travels directly to field situations. In other centers, young visitors took part in lively poster walks, live scientific demonstrations, and practical exercises on body mass index calculation and lab hygiene, learning how everyday health decisions connect to the broader picture of national public health. In Delhi, the spirit of youth innovation was on full display as students showcased creative solutions developed through Atal Tinkering Labs under NITI Aayog, proving that great scientific ideas have no age limit.
As a part of this initiative, ICMR launched the official SHINE website (
https://shine.icmr.org.in/
), providing students with access to resources, program updates and opportunities related to health research. ICMR has also announced a nationwide SHINE school competition, inviting students to identify real-world public health challenges, frame research questions and propose potential solutions. The competition will take the idea of “spending a day as a scientist” a step further by encouraging students to look at the health challenges around them through the lens of scientific inquiry and innovation. Applications are open until 11 September 2026 and can be submitted on the SHINE portal.
The initiative received an encouraging response from participating schools across the country. Teachers welcomed the program for giving students valuable exposure to scientific research and laboratory work beyond the classroom, and suggested that it be held more frequently. The school competition also generated enthusiasm, with one participating school announcing that all its students would take part, with submissions counting towards their internal project assessment during school examination.
Through ICMR-SHINE, thousands of students have moved from simply learning about science to seeing it, experiencing it and asking questions about it. By taking research experiences beyond conventional centers and into schools and field locations across the country, the program is creating opportunities for young minds, regardless of where they live, to encounter science firsthand. ICMR is helping young students develop a scientific outlook, encouraging them to explore science, pursue innovation, and play a role in building a
Swasth
and
Viksit Bharat
.

title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Convenes Two-Day National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan with Participation of Over 160 Representatives from All States and UTs
subtitle:
Stronger Convergence Across Health Programmes and Ministries Needed to Address Anaemia Comprehensively: Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary

New Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB) Digital Platform Launched to Enable Beneficiary-Level Tracking, Treatment Monitoring and Timely Follow-up

States and UTs Recognised for Strong Performance in Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Implementation
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare convened a two-day National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB) on 12–13 August 2026 in New Delhi, bringing together over 160 participants from all States and Union Territories, along with representatives from the Ministries of Education; Women and Child Development; Panchayati Raj; Youth Affairs and Sports; and Tribal Affairs, as well as experts and development and implementation partners. The workshop focused on strengthening the implementation of the revised AMB Abhiyaan and translating the 7×7×7 strategy from policy into effective action on the ground across the country.
The revised AMB Abhiyaan Operational Guidelines, launched by Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda on 29 June 2026 during the Conference of Central Health and Family Welfare (CCHFW), mark a decisive shift in India’s approach to addressing anaemia. Moving beyond a programme focused primarily on supplementation and prophylaxis, the revised guidelines adopt a comprehensive, evidence-based approach centred on testing, case-based management, treatment compliance, consumption of a diverse and nutritious diet, and digital tracking through integrated portals for effective monitoring of beneficiaries.
Addressing the workshop, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, called for stronger convergence across health programmes and closer coordination among ministries to address Anemia comprehensively with better-aligned interventions, screening efforts and service delivery platforms. She also flagged the need to strengthen public awareness and extend supplementation efforts beyond pregnancy to younger age groups through a life-course approach.
Speaking at the Occasion,
Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Health Mission, stressed the importance of effective implementation of the revised AMB Abhiyaan framework at the State, district, facility and community levels. She highlighted the transition from the earlier 6×6×6 framework to the strengthened 7×7×7 approach stressing on improving consumption and compliance to iron supplementation, strengthening beneficiary participation through Jan Bhagidari, and ensuring that State-level innovations and field experiences translate into measurable improvements in programme performance. She further emphasised on digital tracking through the AMB Abhiyaan digital platforms and its linkages to existing portals.
Ms. Meera Srivastava, Joint Secretary (RCH), MoHFW, underscored the need for a paradigm shift from a static, compliance-focused approach to one centred on testing, tracking and timely resolution. She emphasised greater transparency and accurate understanding of prevalence of anemia across beneficiaries, beneficiary-level digital line-listing and data management and integration with other health programmes.
Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research, highlighted the importance of an evidence-based approach to anemia management. He stressed on the importance of evidence-based programme planning, emphasizing on timely testing, severity- and cause-appropriate treatment, repeat testing after three months, healthy iron-rich diets, newer iron formulations where appropriate, and implementation research to strengthen programme effectiveness.
Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, called for a collaborative, holistic and multi-sectoral approach to anemia management. He emphasised on continued importance of micronutrients, iron and protein intake, dietary diversity and understanding underlying diseases and other clinical conditions, all of which effects the outcome of the treatment. He also highlighted the importance of stronger stakeholder engagement, improved treatment and consumption, digital convergence and the use of advanced analytics and AI approaches to identify high-burden clusters and plan targeted action.
A major highlight of the workshop was the launch of the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Application and Portal, aimed at strengthening beneficiary-level tracking, follow-up and management of Anemia. The digital platform is intended to support tracking of beneficiaries identified through screening for monitoring of treatment and compliance, continuity of care, follow-up until resolution. It will also help identify gaps requiring intervention and generation of data for programme review and corrective action.
The workshop also featured the launch of IEC materials and recognition of States/ UTs demonstrating strong performance in implementation of AMB interventions. Dedicated technical sessions covered Anemia screening and testing, digital application and data analytics, prophylaxis and deworming, compliance frameworks, and roles and responsibilities across the delivery chain.
A defining feature of the second day was structured group work by State and UT teams, organised around three thematic tracks: Jan Bhagidari for community ownership, Inter-ministerial coordination, and Implementation challenges. States shared field experiences and practical innovations on each track, with consolidated learnings feeding directly into the way forward for AMB implementation nationally reinforcing the workshop's emphasis on States as co-owners of the Abhiyaan rather than only implementers of it. This was paired with technical sessions on therapeutic management, including oral and intravenous iron protocols, Jan Bhagidari and Eating Right.
The workshop highlighted the need coordinated action across government departments, health-system functionaries, communities, academic and research institutions and partners at every level, to move Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan for a Swasth Viksit Bharat

An important step towards strengthening the domestic REPM manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in the global markets
date:

                13 AUG 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 20 bids through Global Tender on CPP portal for Selection of Manufacturers for establishing integrated Sintered NdFeB Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Facilities under the “Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)”. On 26th November 2025, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the “Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)” with a financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore. The Scheme Notification was issued by MHI on 15.12.2025.
Request For Proposal (RFP) was floated on CPP portal on 20th March 2026. The pre-bid conference was held on 7th April 2026. The last date for receiving bids was 12th August 2026 on CPP portal and the Technical Bids were opened on 13th August 2026 in the presence of the bidders at MHI.
The Scheme, a first-of-its-kind initiative, aims to establish a total capacity of 6,000 Metric Tons Per Annum (MTPA) of integrated Rare Earth Permanent Magnet manufacturing facilities in India, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the global REPM market.
The scheme envisions allocating the total capacity to five beneficiaries through a global competitive bidding process. Each beneficiary will be allotted up to 1,200 MTPA of capacity.
The total duration of the scheme will be 7 years from the date of award, including a 2-year gestation period for setting up an integrated REPM manufacturing facility, and 5 years for incentive disbursement on the sale of REPM.
Rare Earth Permanent Magnets are among the most powerful magnets in the world and are widely used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, high-end electronics, aerospace and defence systems. By building a complete value chain from NdPr oxide to finished magnets in India, the Scheme is expected to significantly reduce import dependence in this sector.
This initiative by the Government of India is a landmark step towards strengthening the domestic REPM manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in global markets. By fostering indigenous capabilities in REPM production, the scheme will not only secure the REPM supply chain for domestic industries but also support the nation’s Net Zero 2070 commitment. It embodies the Government’s unwavering commitment to build a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive, and sustainable industrial base, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

title: Over 5.63 Lakh Villages Covered with Liquid Waste Management Arrangements under SBM(G) Phase II
subtitle: SBM(G) Phase II Focuses on Sustainable Sanitation and Greywater Management in Villages
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Sanitation is a State subject. Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)] Phase II is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by States/UTs in respective jurisdictions. SBM(G) Phase II was launched with effect from 1st April 2020, with the focus on ODF sustainability with Solid & Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) and visual cleanliness in villages i.e. to convert villages from ODF to ODF Plus (Model). Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) monitors the status of Grey Water Management (GWM) under SBM(G) Phase-II as reported by States/UTs on the SBM(G) Integrated Management Information System (IMIS).
As per the information reported by the States/UTs on the SBM(G) IMIS, as on 07.08.2026, out of 5,86,944 villages 5,63,809 villages are reported to have been covered with Liquid Waste Management arrangements.
As per the SBM(G) Phase-II guidelines, various interventions can be undertaken for GWM such as constructions of soak-pit, leach-pit, magic-pit or kitchen garden at household level and Waste Stabilization Ponds, Constructed Wetland, Decentralized Wastewater Treatment System (DEWATS) and Phytorid Technology at community/village level. The SBM(G) IMIS does not capture details of category-wise rural drains (for example: open, closed, kutcha, or pucca drain) or unconnected or inadequate open drains.
As per the data reported by States/UTs on SBM(G) IMIS, as on 07.08.2026, a total of 42,98,194 community GWM assets have been reported. The State/UT-wise details of community GWM assets created, including community soak pits, drainage facilities and community treatment systems, as per data reported by the States/UTs on SBM(G) IMIS may be seen at
Annexure-I
.
DDWS, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India has been providing financial and technical support to the States/UTs for implementation of SBM(G) Phase-II. In each Financial Year, funds are allocated to States/UTs based on their approved Annual Implementation Plan (AIP), past performance and budget availability.
States/UTs can plan for providing sanitation and SLWM facilities under the program as per demand, local preferences, etc. as per their AIP. Apart from budgetary support from DDWS and the corresponding State share, the remaining funds are to be dovetailed by States/UTs from the Finance Commission grants to Rural Local Bodies and MGNREGS/VB-G RAM G. States/UTs can also converge funds from other Central/State schemes, as applicable, CSR funds, MPLADS/MLALADS and revenue generation though business models, etc.
In addition to the SBM(G) Phase II Operational Guidelines, technical manuals and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are provided by DDWS to States/UTs for capacity building of Gram Panchayats on various components of the programme. Under SBM(G) Phase II, for Greywater Management, financial support of up to Rs.280 per capita for villages up to 5000 population and up to Rs.660 per capita for villages above 5000 population is provided. In addition, awareness generation and capacity building interventions are be conducted by States/UTs at various levels to promote community participation, behavioural change and capacity building regarding GWM, including for preventing stagnation of wastewater in rural areas.

title: 75% of Rural Habitations Covered with Sujal Gaon IDs under Jal Jeevan Mission Across States/UTs
subtitle: Sujal Gaon and Sujalam Bharat IDs Strengthen Digital Governance of Rural Water Supply Under JJM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Sujal Gaon ID is a unique identification number assigned under the digital monitoring framework of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 for water supply service area (habitation/s) meeting the prescribed standards and criteria under the Mission. The ID is issued through the national JJM digital platform and the details are communicated to the respective States/UTs through the JJM digital ecosystem. The objective of the Sujal Gaon ID is to facilitate systematic identification, monitoring, reporting, tracking and verification of water supply service area (habitation/s) achieving desired outcomes in rural drinking water service delivery and sustainability. As on 10.08.2026, out of 16,96,213 habitations in the country, Sujal Gaon IDs have been issued to 12,67,808 habitations (75%) across all States/UTs.
Sujalam Bharat has been developed as a federated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) for lifecycle-based and service-oriented management of Rural Piped Water Supply Schemes (RPWSS). It integrates digital asset registries, geospatial mapping and decision-support systems to provide unified visibility of water supply infrastructure. Integrated with the PM GatiShakti platform, it provides a GIS-validated architecture and assigns unique digital identities to rural water supply schemes through Sujalam Bharat IDs.
Sujal Gaon IDs and Sujalam Bharat IDs under the Jal Jeevan Mission provide unique digital identities to service areas and rural water supply schemes, respectively. Their integration with GIS and structured hydraulic linkages enables end-to-end source-to-tap mapping, asset tracking and lifecycle management. This facilitates better planning, monitoring and accountability of existing schemes, helps identify gaps and duplication, and enables data-driven decision-making and effective Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Thus, these digital IDs strengthen transparency and oversight and help reduce irregularities in the implementation of JJM.
This information was provided by
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI V. SOMANNA
in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

title: Union Minister for Law & Justice (I/C) Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal launches revamped India Code Portal at the Legislative Department
subtitle:
Revamped portal to make access to laws simpler, faster and more citizen-centric

AI-assisted search, semantic and speech search, improved navigation and multilingual access among key features
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, today, on 13th August, 2026, launched the revamped India Code Portal at Kartavya Bhavan 2, New Delhi, in the august presence of Shri R. Venkataramani, Attorney General for India, Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, and senior officers of the Legislative Department. Shri Priyank Bharti, Director General, National Informatics Centre (NIC), Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission and senior officers of the NIC were also present on the occasion.
The revamped portal marks an important step in the Government’s continuing endeavour to make access to laws simpler, faster, wider and more citizen-centric, using contemporary digital technologies.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal underscored the importance of the Constitution and of ensuring that laws are easily accessible, understandable and available to all stakeholders. He observed that the India Code Portal serves as a reliable and comprehensive platform for citizen-friendly access to the Constitution, Central Acts, Rules and other legislative information. Highlighting the role of technology in strengthening access to law, he appreciated the dedicated efforts of the officers and officials of the Legislative Department in conceptualising, coordinating and overseeing the revamp, as well as the NIC team for its technical expertise and development support. Shri Meghwal noted that this collaborative effort would significantly enhance the accessibility, transparency and citizen-centric delivery of legislative information.
Shri R. Venkataramani, Attorney General for India, highlighted the transformation from physical to digital access to laws and appreciated the revamped India Code Portal developed by the Legislative Department with several new and user-friendly features. He emphasized the importance of keeping the portal technologically updated and responsive to emerging requirements. He also stressed the responsibility of legislative officers to contribute towards clear, effective and quality legislation and underscored the importance of ensuring wider and convenient access to laws. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Legislative Department and the technical team in developing the revamped portal, which would further strengthen transparency and public access to legislative information.
Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, outlined the evolution of the India Code Portal and the efforts to make authentic and updated legislative information easily accessible to citizens, legal professionals, government departments and other stakeholders. Highlighting the role of technology in improving dissemination and access to laws, he outlined the key features of the revamped portal, including its more user-friendly interface and enhanced search, navigation and accessibility. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Legislative Department and the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and expressed confidence that the revamped platform would significantly strengthen wider and easier public access to reliable legislative information.
Dr Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, introduced the revamped India Code Portal and outlined its key features and the larger vision behind its transformation. He observed that access to law is the first step towards access to justice and that laws must not only be available, but also easy to find, navigate, understand and use. He highlighted that the revamped portal seeks to move India Code beyond being a repository of legislative documents towards becoming an accessible, interconnected and citizen-centric digital gateway to law, with improved search and navigation, linkages between Acts and subordinate legislation, integration with the e-Gazette ecosystem, AI-assisted and semantic search, speech-enabled access and multilingual capabilities. He emphasised that technology should reduce the distance between the law and the citizen and enable legislative information to become more discoverable, interoperable and usable, thereby strengthening transparency, legal awareness and citizen-centric governance.
India Code provides a unified digital repository of Central Acts and their subordinate legislations, State Acts and their subordinate legislations, as well as Union Territory legislations and regulations. The revamped portal significantly enhances the manner in which citizens, legal professionals, researchers, the judiciary and Government can search, navigate and access legislative information through improved and intelligent search capabilities, AI-assisted search and interaction, semantic and speech-based search, easier navigation across legislations, access to amendments and legislative history, linkage of Acts with relevant subordinate legislation, integration with the e-Gazette ecosystem, improved document viewing, QR-enabled access and a structured citizen-feedback mechanism. It also seeks to enable AI-assisted multilingual access to laws in all 22 languages included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, thereby making access to law wider, easier and more citizen-centric across Bharat.
The technological revamp seeks to transform India Code from being merely an online repository of legislation into a digital gateway to law, supported by an increasingly interconnected and citizen-friendly legal information architecture.
The initiative is aligned with the larger objective of leveraging technology for ease of accessing law, transparency, wider citizen participation and improved delivery of legal and public services.
The revamped India Code Portal represents an important step towards building a trusted and technology-enabled legal information ecosystem for Bharat, where laws are increasingly searchable, accessible, interconnected and available to citizens in the language and form most convenient to them.

title: WOMEN FRIENDLY INFRASTRUCTURE IN COURTS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The primary responsibility of development of infrastructure facilities for Judiciary rests with the State Governments. However, to augment the resources of the State and UT Governments, the Central Government has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts since 1993-94. There are five components covered under the Scheme viz. Court Hall, Residential units for Judicial officers, Lawyers’ Hall, Toilet Complexes and Digital Computer Rooms.
Specific aspects including the women-friendly infrastructure in the court halls are within the domain of the High Courts and State Governments. The Building Infrastructure Committee of High Court approves the design of the court halls and projects funded under the CSS. However, the CSS guidelines provide norms and specifications for court halls, which are based on the recommendations of the National Courts Management System (NCMS) Committee of the Supreme Court and norms and practices followed by different States and the CPWD.

title: Government is promoting alternate dispute resolution mechanisms including mediation
subtitle: Government is continuously engaging with various stakeholders including High Courts and NALSA for raising awareness related to mediation and capacity building amongst stakeholders
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government is promoting alternate dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms including mediation, as these mechanisms are less adversarial and are capable of providing a better substitute to the conventional methods of resolving disputes.
Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 provides for mandatory pre-institution mediation and settlement (PIMS) in commercial disputes of specified value, before instituting a suit except in cases in which urgent relief is contemplated by the party. The parties have to therefore first exhaust the mandatory remedy of PIMS before approaching the Court. This is aimed at providing an opportunity to the parties to resolve the commercial disputes through mediation and prevent disputes which are thus amicably settled being taken to courts for adjudication. Authorities established under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 are required to conduct PIMS under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015.
The Mediation Act, 2023, also lays down the statutory framework for mediation to be adopted by parties to a dispute, especially institutional mediation, wherein various stakeholders have also been identified to establish a robust and efficacious mediation ecosystem in the country.  Section 31 of the Act provides for the establishment of Mediation Council of India as a national level body
inter-alia
for promoting mediation as a preferred mode of dispute resolution and for recognising mediation service providers in the country. Also, section 43 of the Act provides for resolution of any dispute which is likely to affect peace, harmony and tranquillity amongst the residents or families of any area or locality through community mediation.
The Government is continuously engaging with various stakeholders including High Courts and NALSA for raising awareness related to mediation and capacity building amongst the stakeholders. In March 2025 a national level Mediation Conference was organised by Ld. Attorney General for India in association with Department of Legal Affairs and India International Arbitration Centre at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
Further, National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) has been taking various steps to promote mediation across the country. These include strengthening ADR Centres and Mediation Centres functioning under the Legal Services Authorities, empanelling and training mediators, promoting pre-litigation and community-based dispute resolution, and implementing the Community Mediation initiative through the State Legal Services Authorities (SLSAs) and District Legal Services Authorities (DLSAs).
NALSA provides funds out of grants in aid received from Govt of India to Mediation and Conciliation Project Committee (MCPC) constituted by Supreme Court of India. MCPC provides training to lawyers to become trained mediators.
Also, NALSA in collaboration with International Academy of Mediators successfully organized a 15 hours Advanced Commercial Mediation Training Program at the Supreme Court of India from 14th October-16th October, 2024 (Batch 1) and from 3rd March to 5th March,2025 (Batch 2). The three-day event brought together experienced legal professionals, mediators, and judges to enhance mediation skills, particularly in handling complex commercial disputes.
As on March, 2026, there are 452 ADR Centres and 1,394 Mediation Centres functioning across the country.  A total of 4,681 Judicial Officers, 10,124 Lawyers, and 753 other Mediators have been trained and deployed as Mediators.
This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF E-COURTS INTEGRATED MISSION MODE PROJECT
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 3:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. The ongoing Phase i.e. [Phase III (2023-27)] envisions a transition towards digital, paperless and more intelligent courts through large-scale digitisation of records, wider use of virtual hearings, deeper interoperability across justice institutions and adoption of emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI). The details of progress achieved under Phase – III of the project is at
Annexure – I.
The implementation of the eCourts Mission Mode Project has improved case management through the Case Information System (CIS) 4.0 and the JustIS application, enabling Judges to digitally manage and monitor cases. It has strengthened digital filing through the e-Filing system, which facilitates online filing of cases and related applications, and e-Payments for online payment of court fees. Further, video conferencing facilities have enabled virtual and hybrid court hearings across the implemented courts. These initiatives have enhanced the efficiency, accessibility and transparency of judicial administration and service delivery.
Under the eCourts Mission Mode Project, various steps have been undertaken to improve digital literacy and awareness among litigants and lawyers, including those in Andhra Pradesh. These include training programmes, capacity-building workshops, user manuals, video tutorials and outreach initiatives conducted through the High Courts and the State Judicial Academies.
Further, eSewa Kendras assist litigants and advocates in registration on the e-Filing portal, scanning and uploading of petitions, online payment of court fees, case status enquiries, certified copy applications, video conferencing and access to other digital court services. In addition, the eCourts services, District Court websites and eCourts mobile application provide online access to case status, cause lists, judgments, orders and other court-related information. These initiatives promote digital literacy, enhance awareness and facilitate wider access to eCourts services.

2026 and the Income-Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 which were promulgated by the President before Monsoon Session, were considered and passed by both the Houses.
Demands for Excess Grants for the year 2022-23 were taken up and the related Appropriation Bill was introduced, considered and passed by Lok Sabha on 04.08.2026 and returned by the Rajya Sabha on 06.08.2026.
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was referred to the Joint Committee of the Houses for examination and report.
In order to address, with immediacy, the concerns of students relating to public examinations,
the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026
was introduced to amend the parent Act of 2024 as a major initiative to strengthen the integrity and credibility of the public examination system. The Bill seeks to ensure speedy investigation and time-bound trial of offences under the Act; empower State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to designate Special Fast Track Courts and appoint Special Public Prosecutors; mandate completion of investigations within two months and trials within three months; enable the Central Government to constitute Special Task Forces for investigation, wherever necessary; enhance penalties for offences; and provide for a time-bound appellate  mechanism before a Division Bench of the High Court. The Bill was passed by both Houses of Parliament and has been assented to by the President.
Some other major Bills passed by both Houses during the Session are as under:
The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026
seeks to amend the Act of 1971 to bring
Vande Mataram
, honoured as the National Song, within the ambit of Section 3 of
The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 and
proposes to make it an offence to intentionally prevent the singing of
Vande Mataram
or cause disturbance to any assembly engaged in its singing, thereby extending legal protection to the National Song and making such acts punishable under the Act.
The Registration of
Births and Deaths
(Amendment) Bill,
2026
seeks to amend the parent Act of 1969 to make provisions for delayed registration of births and deaths more stringent by prescribing a streamlined verification mechanism. The Bill provides for registration after one year and up to two years only with the approval of the competent Executive Magistrate, and after two years only with the approval of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
Ø
The Micro, Small
and Medium
Enterprises
Development
(Amendment) Bill,
2026
seeks to amend the Act of 2006 to provide for a national digital platform for free and voluntary registration of MSMEs and strengthen the MSME sector by improving access to finance, ensuring faster adjudication of delayed payment disputes of micro and small enterprises, promoting ease of doing business, and decriminalizing offences regarding contravention of certain provisions, replacing conviction-based fines with graded penalties by including warning at the first instance.
Ø
The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026
seeks to expand the scope of the definition of “bankers’ books” to include all forms of records maintained by banks, whether in physical, electronic, digital, virtual, cloud-based or in any other form, thereby providing a comprehensive, technology-neutral and future-ready legal framework. It standardises certificates and recognises manual, digital and electronic authentication, while enabling electronic records to be produced physically or electronically. It further empowers the Central Government to extend coverage across the financial sector and defines “special cause” for judicial production.
Ø
The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026
seeks
to amend the First Schedule to the Constitution by altering the name of State of “Kerala” as “Keralam” in accordance with article 3 of the Constitution.
Ø
The
National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026
seeks to amend the National Co-operative Development Corporation Act, 1962 to
expand the definition of “foodstuffs” to include any other food items as may be notified by the Central Government, remove the geographical restriction applicable to industrial goods, strengthen the co-operative sector by updating statutory references, removing obsolete provisions, and empowering the Corporation with necessary incidental powers. These measures will facilitate the collection and sharing of credit and other relevant information with authorized institutions, while providing greater flexibility, legal clarity and operational efficiency and enable timely, direct and responsive financial assistance for co-operative development.
Ø
The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026
seeks
to improve the efficiency, ensure independence, transparency, and uniformity in the qualifications, appointment, terms and conditions of service of Chairpersons and Members of various Tribunals, the administration and functioning of the Tribunals, to establish a National Tribunals Commission and to make consequential amendments in related enactments and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
Ø
The
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
seeks to amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 to provide certainty, stability and predictability in the fiscal regime in the mineral sector, thereby giving impetus to national economic growth which would facilitate the aims of Atmanirbhar Bharat and ultimately attaining the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: Factual Position Regarding Media Report on Disposal of Cases by CIC
subtitle: CIC Disposes of 768 Cases in August up to 12 August, Against Three Reported in Media Report
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Information Commission (CIC) has taken note of a media report concerning the disposal of Second Appeals and Complaints during August 2026 and considers it necessary to place the factual position before the public.
The Commission clarifies that the figures relating to disposal of cases during August 2026, as reflected in the said news report, do not represent the actual disposal of cases by the Commission up to 12 August 2026. As against the figure of
three appeals
reported as having been disposed of during August, the Commission has in fact
disposed of 768 cases up to 12 August 2026 in the current month
. The decisions in the disposed cases are also being simultaneously dispatched by post to the concerned parties.
The Second Appeals and Complaints Portal of the Commission has been undergoing upgradation since
2 August 2026
. Consequently, the data relating to cases admitted and disposed of, which is automatically updated on the Commission’s website from the said portal, has remained updated only up to
1 August 2026
. A notice regarding the portal upgradation had already been displayed on the Commission’s website and the Second Appeals and Complaints Portal on
24 July 2026
.
It is important to clarify that the non-updation of the portal data has
not affected the functioning of the Commission or the conduct of hearings
. Hearings before the Commission have continued as usual during the period of portal upgradation.
The Commission therefore wishes to emphasise that
the figures presently visible on its website during the portal-upgradation period should not be construed as reflecting the actual disposal of cases during August 2026
.
The upgradation of the Second Appeals and Complaints Portal is being undertaken with the objective of
improving the experience of RTI applicants and other stakeholders using the Commission’s online services
. The upgraded portal is intended to provide a more efficient and user-friendly digital interface for accessing and managing information relating to Second Appeals and Complaints.
The upgradation will also facilitate more efficient updating and availability of case-related information on the Commission’s website and portal, thereby making it easier for stakeholders to access current information regarding their cases.
The upgraded Second Appeals and Complaints Portal is expected to be
live and operational from 17 August 2026
, following which the relevant case data is expected to be updated on the Commission’s website and portal.
The Commission remains committed to transparency and to providing accurate and verifiable information regarding its functioning. It will continue to make relevant case-disposal data available to stakeholders through its website and portal once the upgradation process is completed.
*****
NKR/AV

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 1:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Presently 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. The Government of West Bengal has not yet signed the tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) under Mission Karmayogi.
So far, eight draft Capacity Building Plans (CBPs) have been prepared for Government of West Bengal's priority departments. The iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform hosts over 5,600 courses covering domain, functional and behavioural competencies. These courses are available for consumption for all registered users including those from West Bengal. As on date, 10,493 course completions have been recorded by learners from West Bengal. Further, all employees of the Central Government and officers of the All India Services, including those serving in West Bengal have to mandatorily complete prescribed courses annually on iGOT which gets reflected in their respective APARs for the corresponding period.
The DoPT, along with the other implementing agencies of Mission Karmayogi – Capacity Building Commission (CBC), and SPV Karmayogi Bharat (KB) are supporting the Government of West Bengal in its capacity building initiatives including handholding for the adoption of the role-based competency framework, onboarding on the iGOT platform, and integrating iGOT with other HR platforms/tools. A Programme Coordinator from CBC and an Assistant Manager from KB serve as Nodal Officers for the state of West Bengal for this purpose. DoPT also supports targeted capacity building activities in all states/UTs, including West Bengal, through the Training for All (TFA) scheme.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ZERO LITIGATION PENSION ECOSYSTEM
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 1:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare is the nodal Department for formulation of policies relating to pension and other retirement benefits of Central Government Civil employees. The 2nd National Workshop on Pension Litigation was convened in pursuance of Government's directives on effective and efficient management of litigation with focus on enhancing coordination and strengthening the capacity/skills of the Nodal officers and panel lawyers of all the Ministries/Departments handling Pension related litigation and its monitoring. It had deliberations and presentations from speakers on the best practices, systemic reforms and grievance redressals to minimize pension litigation towards welfare of pensioners and good governance. The Compendium of case laws and flyer, launched in the Workshop, outlined the best practices in handling pension litigation and recent judicial pronouncements in recurring pension litigation matters providing a comprehensive overview of the concerned pension related policies.
The compendium and flyer underscored the importance of a coordinated approach to managing pension litigation. Pension litigation is not centrally handled by any Department, it is handled on behalf of the Central Government separately by all respective Departments. For minimising litigation, Special Campaign 3 was also launched, wherein focus is on the redressal of the long pending grievances/claims and the issues. This campaign along with other initiatives viz. Pension Adalats and Inter-Ministerial Review Meetings on long pending grievances is an attempt to resolve the grievances, thereby obviating the need to approach courts of law with the resultant effect of reduction in litigation. Further, the Department, based on the clarification and advices sought by various Ministries and Departments, issues Office Memoranda to clarify the rule position to bring ease in the life of the pensioners including super-senior pensioners. The Department, has issued the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 revised it further by CCS(Pension) Rules, 2021. To ease eligibility conditions of family pensioners, Rule 50 of the said Rules (erstwhile Rule 54 of Rules of 1972) has been provided for various categories of family pensioners including divorced and disabled daughters.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

title: New computer model can help trace magnetic energy builds up & forecast impact of resulting CMEs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A multi-institutional team of scientists have developed a three-dimensional computer simulation model that can bring scientists a step closer to forecasting the arrival and impact of Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) before they reach Earth.
CMEs are among the most dramatic and powerful events in our solar system — gigantic eruptions of magnetized plasma hurled from the Sun at millions of kilometres per hour. When directed toward Earth, they can damage satellite systems, disrupt power grids, and interfere with global communications. At the heart of these eruptions lie magnetic flux ropes (MFRs), which are twisted bundles of magnetic field lines embedd
ed in the
plasma
, and are
widely regarded as the primary triggers of CMEs. Yet, how the magnetic energy builds up, and is then release
d
during CMEs has remained one of solar physics' most stubborn mysteries through the violent expulsion has been poorly understood until now.
Fig 1:
Snapshots from our simulation showing a twisted magnetic structure — called a flux rope — rising through the Sun's outer atmosphere. The red threads represent the Sun's background magnetic field, while blue, green, and cyan threads trace the emerging rope from its core outward. The full animation covers about 20 hours of solar time and ends with the rope being violently ejected into space.
In order to trace the evolution of the magnetic energy to CMEs researchers at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Govt. of India, al
o
ng with their collaborator
s
, have developed sophisticated three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computer simulation model.
This model
traces, step by step, how the reconnection flux changes as a magnetic flux rope rises, stretches the surrounding ambient magnetic field, and ultimately erupts. The model begins with a realistic coronal setup of a solar atmosphere,
which is
threaded by a magnetic field configuration resembling a coronal streamer
in observation
.
A
twisted magnetic flux rope is gradually introduced into this
from below, mimicking how new magnetic flux emerges from beneath the solar surface.
Fig 2:
The reconnection engine, caught in the act. The white surface (panel a) marks the current sheet — where the Sun's magnetic field lines snap and reconnect, releasing the energy that launches a CME. The S-shaped field lines in panels (b) and (c) are the magnetic threads passing through this energy release site.
The computational work in this study was performed on the NOVA HPC facility. This high-performance computing infrastructure is hosted at the data center of the IIA.
As the flux rope rises, the team observed in their c
omputer models that
the overlying magnetic field
is
significantly stretched and compressed beneath it. Reconnection does not begin explosively.
I
nstead, it starts quietly with the slow formation of a thin sheet of strong electric cur
rent
, a thin layer where opposing magnetic fields are pushed together. Over time, this process intensifies, culminating in the impulsive, large-scale expulsion of the flux rope.
What makes this study published in
Astrophysical Journal
particularly compelling is its dual approach. The researchers not only simulated two successive flux rope eruptions in their model, but also cross-validated their findings with another researcher from the University of Helsinki, Finland, who teamed up with the Indian group to contribute analysis based on observational data from NASA's Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) and the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA), two of the most powerful instruments currently observing the Sun.
Fig 3
: Seeing reconnection from Earth. Left: the flash of the flare. Right: its magnetic footprint — color-coded ribbons sweeping outward across the Sun's surface over 36 minutes. The area swept by these ribbons is our observational measure of how much magnetic flux was reconnected during the eruption.
The comparison between simulation and observation revealed a striking result: the rate of magnetic reconnection correlates the acceleration of the CME in a clear, monotonic fashion
,
meaning that as reconnection speeds up, so does the eruption, from start to finish. This finding establishes reconnection flux as a critical factor in determining not just whether a CME erupts, but how fast and how energetically it does so.
This work by the team comprising Dr. Samriddhi Sankar Maity (Postdoc at NASA & Georgia State University, USA), Dr. Piyali Chatterjee, IIA and Mr. Ijas S Mytheen (PhD student, Eotvos University, Hungary) and Dr. Ranadeep Sarkar from the University of Helsinki, Finland, offers important new insight into the chain of events that transforms a slowly building magnetic structure into one of
the
powerful
explosions in
our solar system
.
Publication link:
https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-4357/ae3d9a
.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING CSIR GOVERNANCE AND RESEARCH
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 AUG 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
CSIR has established institutional mechanisms to promote coordination among its constituent laboratories, academia, industry and other stakeholders for research, technology development and commercialisation of indigenous technologies. CSIR, through its constituent laboratories/institutes, collaborates with academia and industry for R&D in areas of mutual interest and complementary expertise. Dedicated Business Development Groups (BDGs) are functional both at the laboratory level and at CSIR Headquarters to facilitate industry engagement, technology transfer, licensing of technologies, contract research, consultancy, collaborative R&D and adoption of CSIR-developed technologies and products.
Technology transfer and commercialisation activities are supported through a structured framework comprising identification of industry partners, execution of technology licensing agreements, intellectual property management, technical handholding during technology absorption, and post-transfer support, wherever required. CSIR laboratories also maintain regular engagement with industry through technology demonstrations, industry interactions, buyer-seller meets, technology showcases, startup conclaves, innovation workshops and participation in national and international technology exhibitions to enhance industry outreach and facilitate commercialisation. In addition, incubation centres established at selected CSIR laboratories provide an enabling ecosystem for innovation-based enterprises by offering access to specialised R&D infrastructure, prototyping and pilot-scale facilities, advanced analytical and testing equipment, scientific and technical mentoring, consultancy services, intellectual property facilitation, capacity building, entrepreneurship support and networking opportunities with investors, industry and other innovation stakeholders. These initiatives facilitate the translation of research outcomes into commercially viable technologies and products.
The Government continuously studies and draws upon global best practices, including those followed by leading research and innovation ecosystems, for strengthening the functioning of national research institutions, wherever considered appropriate.
CSIR actively collaborates with Central Ministries, State Governments, PSUs, industry, academia and other stakeholders through research partnerships, technology transfer, licensing agreements, pilot demonstrations, consultancy and capacity-building initiatives to facilitate the adoption and commercialization of indigenous technologies. The adoption of CSIR-developed technologies is undertaken by the respective user agencies based on their functional requirements and techno-commercial considerations.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
